purpose: Prevent new normative concepts from entering Mimer until semantic absence has been falsified against existing canonical semantics.
normative_rules: A proposed normative concept MUST remain UNRESOLVED until every stop question has an evidence-backed answer.
No implementation, schema, artifact family or enum MAY be justified by a predicted disposition.
DERIVABLE means the proposed semantics can be deterministically obtained from existing canonical artifacts, policies or verified closures without adding irreducible meaning.
SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE means existing canonical semantics already express the same normative meaning, even if representation or naming differs.
MECHANISM_ONLY means the proposal is an implementation or verification mechanism and MUST NOT be promoted to a new normative semantic concept solely because it is useful operationally.
WRONG_ABSTRACTION_LEVEL means the proposal generalizes beyond demonstrated use cases or specializes semantics that belong at an existing broader boundary.
IRREDUCIBLE_SEMANTIC is permitted only after DERIVABLE, SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE, MECHANISM_ONLY and WRONG_ABSTRACTION_LEVEL have been falsified with repository evidence.
BLOCKED_BY_PRECONDITION means evaluation cannot proceed because an existing constitutional or verification guarantee is missing, ambiguous or contradicted.
A proposal that changes, weakens, depends on, or silently assumes an existing constitutional guarantee MUST stop as BLOCKED_BY_PRECONDITION until that guarantee is explicitly proved or amended.
Unknown, absent or unverified evidence MUST NOT be interpreted as satisfying semantic absence or a positive permission.

stop_questions.question: Does an existing canonical artifact, binding, invariant, policy or verified closure already express this meaning?
Can the proposed meaning be deterministically derived from existing canonical inputs without introducing new normative state?
Is the proposal semantically duplicate with an existing concept despite different naming or representation?
Is the proposal only a mechanism, cache, projection, verifier output or operational convenience rather than irreducible semantics?
Is the proposal at the wrong abstraction level, including premature generalization before a second demonstrated use case?
Does the proposal change, weaken, depend on, or silently assume an existing constitutional or verification guarantee?
